tree_state: all files listed under artifacts are uncommitted at recording time and are committed in the commit that follows this record; the recorded commit is its parent
summary: EP0-only polled DWC3 device engine (freestanding C, 11026 bytes of text for aarch64), a DWC3 + non-coherent-cache + USB-host model, 54 engine tests with 13 seeded engine defects, and the unattended collector s24_logd.py writing NAT-016 archives, with 46 tests and a 43/43 mutation check. Nothing was run on the phone; the model is a reading of the vendor driver.

acceptance.1_engine: engine/usbmon.c compiles for aarch64-freestanding with -Wall -Wextra -Werror (aarch64-build exit 0, 11026 bytes text, no undefined symbols checked by test_engine.test_the_engine_is_freestanding_aarch64_code); no interrupts, no allocation, one event buffer, at most two TRBs; descriptors for VID 0x1209/PID 0x0001, vendor class, no endpoints; vendor control-IN GET_INFO/READ_RING/GET_EXC, SET_NONCE; register/TRB constants cross-checked against the pinned vendor core.h/gadget.h by test_engine (GPL-2.0, attribution in dwc3_regs.h).
acceptance.2_model_and_tests: model/model.c simulates register file, endpoint commands, event buffer, TRB processing, cache and a USB host stub; test_engine.py (54 tests, exit 0) covers descriptor reads, partial reads, ring wrap/overrun markers, an exception frame, requests while holding, malformed SETUPs, resets in every stage; 13 seeded engine defects are each caught (SeededDefectTests).
acceptance.3_collector: s24_logd.py waits unattended, sends a fresh nonce, pulls the ring and the exception frame, writes NAT-016 frames through archive.py with boot_id = host nonce + device boot block, bridges short disconnects, and records every loss as a named drop; test_logd.py (46 tests, exit 0) runs it against the model and the real archive; mutate_logd.py killed 43 of 43 seeded collector defects; the CLI with real pyusb and no device ends outcome incomplete with exit 2 (cli-smoke).

established: The engine, the protocol constants in usbmon_proto.py and engine/usbmon.h, the register constants in dwc3_regs.h and the vendor core.h/gadget.h at the pin agree (tests fail on any differing value).

Against the model the engine enumerates, serves GET_INFO/READ_RING/GET_EXC/SET_NONCE, keeps the stream consistent through wraps, 32-bit offset boundaries, interrupted appends and bus resets, and obeys the DMA discipline under a worst-case prefetcher; each of 13 seeded defects is detected.

The collector turns the engine's stream into NAT-016 frames without loss or duplication on the good path, names every kind of loss it can see, detects a device restart without a disconnect, bridges short disconnects, never opens a Samsung vendor id, and every one of 43 seeded collector defects makes its tests fail.
The model tests found one real engine defect: the vendor-request type constant (0x20 class instead of 0x40 vendor), now fixed and guarded.
not_established: Anything about the real S24: that the DWC3 at 0x17900000 answers this register sequence, that PHY/repeater/clock prerequisites (NAT-040 U1-U8) can be met by the loader, that dc civac is the right cache maintenance for the loader's mapping, that libusb accepts a device with no interface endpoints, that the host sees 1209:0001.
That the model is faithful: it encodes one reading of the vendor dwc3 driver; a misreading shared by engine and model is invisible to these tests.
Unattended retrieval of a real native run (NAT-043's criterion); the collector has not seen real USB hardware, only pyusb's error mapping through a fake usb.core and a no-device run.

That the stop-reason mapping (a deliberate deadline passed to archive.finish as eof) is the right long-term semantics for NAT-016 consumers; it is documented, and the true reason is in events.jsonl and collector-summary.json.
PEEK is reserved and unimplemented; polling stops once XNU runs unless the kernel keeps calling the engine.
